text_blocks.snippet: Scams targeting Central Illinois residents frequently involve fake text messages about unpaid traffic or tollway violations, utility switch tricks, and online shopping fraud.

list.snippet:
Fake Toll and Traffic Texts: Scammers send text messages pretending to be the Illinois Secretary of State or transportation departments, claiming you owe fines for missed tolls or tickets and threatening license suspension
.
Utility Slamming: Impostors call or visit claiming to represent local utility providers to trick you into switching your electricity or gas supplier.
Package Delivery Texts: Fraudulent texts claim a delivery is delayed or held due to a missing address, asking for credit card details or personal info via a link.
Online Purchase & Pet Scams: Fake classifieds or websites take money for goods or companion pets that never arrive.
Do not click links in unexpected text messages or emails regarding government fines or deliveries. State agencies never use text messages to demand payment.
Verify independently by looking up official phone numbers or websites rather than using contacts provided in suspicious messages.
Report fraud or check current local alerts through the Better Business Bureau of Central Illinois or forward suspicious state-related texts to scamalertils.gov.
